newsitem.title: FRANCE: Trichet says low inflation allowed rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Trichet says low inflation allowed rate cut.

text.p: Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet said France's low inflation permitted the bank's 10 basis point cut in the intervention rate to 3.25 percent today.
He told LCI television the interest rate was currently "extremely low" and at the lowest level for more than half a century.

He also said the rate cut had been possible because of regained confidence in the franc in the foreign exchange markets and the governments commitment, contained in Wednesday's 1997 budget, that it will bring the state deficit to three percent of GDP in 1997.

"The first reason...is that we have a very good result inflation wise. The previous month (July) we hade a 2.3 percent rise in prices, we have now (August) 1.7 percent. We are fully in line with our strategy which was, for the monetary council, to say that the price rises needed to be less than two percent at the end of the year," he said.
